tasks.words: A colleague sent me this link to one of the files in our payments code. What uses this file?
tasks.rightAnswer: Contracts/IPaymentService.cs is used by four files: Hub/PaymentHub.cs and PaymentService/PaymentService.cs (code), and Hub/App.config and PaymentService/App.config (configuration that names the service contract). Naming the two code files and the two configuration files is a full answer; the code files alone is a partial one.

tasks.words: Can you open the PaymentService folder in this map and tell me how the files in it connect?
tasks.rightAnswer: PaymentService/ holds App.config, PaymentService.cs, PaymentService.csproj and a Data/ subfolder (Payment.cs, PaymentsContext.cs, PostPaymentRow.cs). Inside: PaymentService.cs uses Payment.cs, PostPaymentRow.cs and PaymentsContext.cs; PaymentsContext.cs uses Payment.cs, PostPaymentRow.cs and App.config (its PaymentsDb connection string); App.config names PaymentService.cs as the service, which closes a cycle PaymentService.cs -> PaymentsContext.cs -> App.config -> PaymentService.cs; PaymentService.csproj connects to nothing inside the folder. Outside: PaymentService.cs uses four Contracts files (IPaymentService, PaymentQuery, PaymentRequest, PaymentResult); App.config names Contracts/IPaymentService.cs and is used by Hub/App.config; Payment.cs and PaymentsContext.cs reach the SQL Server scripts; the .csproj references Contracts.csproj. On the World Map the folder is the box named "payments", not PaymentService: finding it is part of the task. A full answer has the inside connections with their directions and says PaymentService.cs is the hub; the cycle and the outside connections are a plus.

tasks.words: This is a map of our payments system. When someone submits a payment on the web page, what happens to it? Name each piece of the system it passes through, in order, until it is stored.
tasks.rightAnswer: Written 2026-11-21 before any run, from the sample's source and README, not from the map. The submitted payment goes: (1) Portal/Pages/Default.aspx, the page with the payment form, which loads (2) Portal/Scripts/portal.js; on submit it POSTs JSON to the portal's own route api/payments, received by (3) Portal/Controllers/PaymentsController.cs, which calls (4) Portal/Services/GatewayClient.cs; that POSTs to the gateway's api/payments at Portal.GatewayBaseUrl (Portal/Web.config, read through Portal/App_Code/Globals.cs). In the gateway, (5) Gateway/Controllers/PaymentsController.cs stamps the request's Workload and Environment from Gateway/GatewaySettings.cs (Gateway/Web.config) and calls (6) Gateway/Wcf/HubProxy.cs, which opens the WCF client endpoint "PaymentHub" in (7) Gateway/Web.config, net.tcp://hub.onprem.example:8731/PaymentHub, over the IPsec tunnel from the cloud to on-prem. (8) Hub/App.config hosts that address as the service (9) Hub/PaymentHub.cs, which does no payment work: it asks (10) Hub/ServiceRouting.cs for the endpoint name PaymentService.<Workload>.<Environment> (PaymentService.Consumer.Production), a client endpoint in Hub/App.config at net.tcp://payments.onprem.example:8732/PaymentService, and forwards the call. (11) PaymentService/App.config hosts that address as (12) PaymentService/PaymentService.cs, whose Post opens (13) PaymentService/Data/PaymentsContext.cs (connection string PaymentsDb in PaymentService/App.config) and calls PostPayment, which EXECs (14) Database/SqlServer/dbo.usp_PostPayment.sql; the procedure INSERTs the payment into (15) the SQL Server table dbo.Payment (Database/SqlServer/dbo.Payment.sql), where it is stored, and reads the account balance from (16) the Oracle table CENTRAL.ACCOUNT (Database/Oracle/CENTRAL.ACCOUNT.sql) through the ORACLE_CENTRAL linked server; the row returns as PaymentService/Data/PostPaymentRow.cs. The Contracts files (PaymentRequest, PaymentResult, IPaymentHub, IPaymentService) carry the message from gateway to service. A full answer names, in this order, the page and its script, the portal's controller and its gateway client, the gateway (controller and hub proxy), the hub with its routing, the payment service and its data context, the stored procedure, and the dbo.Payment table; the Oracle read and the configuration files that carry each hop are a plus. Partly: the right order with a piece missing or merged (the portal's own controller skipped, the hub's routing not named, or the answer stopping at the service or the database without the table). Wrong: an order that contradicts the flow, or the payment said to be stored somewhere else. On the built map (2026-11-21) every hop above is a recorded connection in the direction of the flow except Hub/PaymentHub.cs to Hub/App.config (the hub's code naming the client endpoint that ServiceRouting builds): the hub's code leads on the map only to ServiceRouting.cs, and the onward path runs configuration to configuration, Gateway/Web.config -> Hub/App.config -> PaymentService/App.config -> PaymentService.cs.
